strings.name: Rajiv Bajaj
strings.role: Managing Director and CEO of Bajaj Auto
strings.summary: Rajiv Bajaj is an Indian automotive executive who began working at Bajaj Auto in 1990 and became Managing Director in 2005. He advanced a motorcycle strategy centered on brands such as Pulsar and international expansion. During his tenure, the company launched electric Chetak and dual-fuel CNG Freedom models and gained indirect control of the KTM group.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 17 November 2026. Distinguish Managing Director from chairman, Bajaj Group from the automotive company, and product launches and completed transactions from commercial outcomes. The master’s graduation year is omitted because official sources conflict.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced Bajaj Auto’s brand and motorcycle strategy, expanding Indian manufacturing’s international markets.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned a mechanical engineering degree from the University of Pune in 1988 and a master’s in manufacturing systems engineering from the University of Warwick.
strings.facts.f2.label: Current role
strings.facts.f2.value: Managing Director and CEO of Bajaj Auto; the new term beginning in 2025 is scheduled to run through 31 March 2030. This is distinct from the chairman’s role.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Motorcycle transformation through brands
strings.highlights.h1.text: Helped develop brands such as Pulsar, combining brand positioning and production platforms for international markets; results reflect the shared work of management, R&D and manufacturing teams.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Multiple powertrain approaches and international operations
strings.highlights.h2.text: During his tenure, the company expanded electric and CNG products and gained indirect control of the KTM group in 2025; product prospects and restructuring outcomes require continuing assessment.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Participation in group centenary event
strings.timeline.t1.text: Discussed consistency between words and actions and trust at Bajaj Group’s Mumbai event; this was not the automotive company’s centenary.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Indirect control of the KTM group
strings.timeline.t2.text: Through its Dutch subsidiary, the company acquired the remaining 50.1% of an intermediate holding company, resulting in a 74.9% effective interest in the KTM group.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Beginning a new management term
strings.timeline.t3.text: A new five-year term as Managing Director and CEO took effect; shareholders approved it on 30 April.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Freedom 125 launch
strings.timeline.t4.text: The company introduced a motorcycle that switches between compressed natural gas and petrol; it is not a zero-emission electric vehicle.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Commercial launch of electric Chetak
strings.timeline.t5.text: The company launched an electric scooter, with bookings opening the following day; distinguish the earlier unveiling from actual deliveries.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becoming Managing Director
strings.timeline.t6.text: Advanced from earlier management roles to Managing Director of Bajaj Auto, continuing to develop its motorcycle strategy.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Pulsar brand launch
strings.timeline.t7.text: The company introduced the Pulsar motorcycle range, an important product in the brand transformation he promoted; he was not yet Managing Director.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Starting his Bajaj Auto career
strings.timeline.t8.text: Initially worked in manufacturing and supply chains, later moving into R&D and engineering, then marketing and sales.
